raw: After Part 2 of the Transport (Safety Schemes Compliance and Enforcement) Act 2014 insert— "Part 2A—Investigatory powers— Chief Investigator, Transport Safety Division 1—Object 49A Object The object of this Part is to improve public transport and marine safety by providing for the independent investigation of public transport safety matters and marine safety matters by the Chief Investigator, Transport Safety. Division 2—Entry and boarding 49B Entry into public transport premises, marine premises, rolling stock or bus or boarding vessel (1) The Chief Investigator, for the purpose of carrying out an investigation into a public transport safety matter or marine safety matter, may at any time— (a) enter a place that is, or that the Chief Investigator reasonably suspects is— (i) public transport premises; or (ii) marine premises; or (b) enter rolling stock or a bus while it is in use; or (c) board a vessel while it is in use. (2) If the Chief Investigator enters a place under subsection (1) and it is not public transport premises or marine premises, the Chief Investigator must leave the place immediately. (3) An entry or boarding may be made under subsection (1) with or without the consent of the person with control or management of the place, rolling stock, bus or vessel. (4) If the Chief Investigator exercises a power of entry or boarding under this section without the owner or occupier of the public transport premises or marine premises or adjoining place or person with the control or management of the rolling stock, bus or vessel being present, the Chief Investigator must, on leaving the premises, place, rolling stock, bus or vessel, leave a notice setting out— (a) the time of entry; and (b) the purpose of entry; and (c) a description of things done while on the premises, rolling stock, bus or vessel; and (d) the time of departure; and (e) the procedure for contacting the Chief Investigator for further details of the entry or boarding. (5) The Chief Investigator may also enter any place, rolling stock or bus or board a vessel if the entry or boarding is authorised by a search warrant. Subsection (4) does not apply in respect of that kind of entry. 49C Notification of entry (1) The Chief Investigator may enter a place, rolling stock or bus or board a vessel under section 49B without prior notice to any person. (2) The Chief Investigator must, as soon as practicable after entry to a place that is, or that the Chief Investigator reasonably suspects is, public transport premises or marine premises take all reasonable steps to notify the person with control or management of the premises of the Chief Investigator's entry. (3) The Chief Investigator must, as soon as practicable after entering rolling stock or a bus or boarding a vessel, take all reasonable steps to notify the operator and driver of the rolling stock or bus or master of the vessel of the Chief Investigator's entry or boarding. (4) However, the Chief Investigator is not required to notify any person if to do so would— (a) defeat the purpose for which the place, rolling stock or bus was entered or the vessel was boarded; or (b) cause unreasonable delay. Division 3—Powers on entry and boarding 49D General powers on entry or boarding (1) If the Chief Investigator enters public transport premises or marine premises or rolling stock or bus or boards a vessel under section 49B, the Chief Investigator may do any of the following— (a) search, inspect and examine the premises, rolling stock, bus or vessel; (b) make inquiries at the premises or on the rolling stock, bus or vessel; (c) inspect, examine or copy any thing (including a document) at the premises or on the rolling stock, bus or vessel; (d) bring to the premises or onto the rolling stock, bus or vessel, and use at the premises or on the rolling stock, bus or vessel, any equipment or materials that may be required; (e) enter or open, using reasonable force— (i) rail infrastructure, a road vehicle or other thing at the railway premises; or (ii) the rolling stock, bus or vessel or a thing on the rolling stock bus or vessel— to examine the infrastructure, rolling stock, road vehicle, bus, vessel or other thing; (f) take measurements, make surveys and take levels at the premises and, for those purposes, dig trenches, break up the soil and set up any posts, stakes or markers at the premises; (g) conduct tests and make sketches or recordings (including photographs, films, audio, video, digital or other recordings)— (i) at the premises or on or of any road vehicle at the premises; or (ii) on or of rolling stock or a bus or vessel; (h) mark, tag or otherwise identify— (i) a road vehicle or other thing at the premises; or (ii) rolling stock or a bus or vessel or a thing on the rolling stock, bus or vessel; (i) seize any thing (including a document)— (i) at the premises or in a road vehicle at the premises; or (ii) on the rolling stock, bus or vessel— if the Chief Investigator reasonably believes that the seizure of the thing is necessary for the purpose of carrying out an investigation into a public transport safety matter or a marine safety matter; (j) seize any thing at the premises or on the rolling stock, bus or vessel if the Chief Investigator believes on reasonable grounds that it is necessary to seize the thing in order to prevent its concealment, loss or destruction; (k) take and remove for analysis, testing or examination a sample of any substance or thing from the premises or the rolling stock, bus or vessel without paying for it; (l) require the following persons to give the Chief Investigator reasonable help to exercise the Chief Investigator's powers under paragraphs (a) to (k)— (i) a person at the public transport premises or marine premises; (ii) a rail safety worker at railway premises or on rolling stock; (iii) the driver of the bus; (iv) the master or a member of the crew of the vessel; (m) exercise any power that is reasonably necessary to be exercised by the Chief Investigator for the purposes of an investigation into a public transport safety matter or a marine safety matter. (2) A person required to give reasonable help under subsection (1)(l) must not, without reasonable excuse, fail to comply with the requirement. Penalty: In the case of a natural person, 60 penalty units; In the case of a body corporate, 300 penalty units. (3) In this section— reasonable help includes— (a) assistance to enable the Chief Investigator to find and gain access to electronically stored material and information at the public transport premises or marine premises or on the rolling stock, bus or vessel; and (b) unloading rolling stock at the public transport premises; and (c) running the engine of— (i) a locomotive at the public transport premises; or (ii) the bus; and (d) operating the vessel; and (e) driving a train, tram or bus; and (f) giving the Chief Investigator assistance to enter any rail infrastructure or any part of rail infrastructure, or open rolling stock or any part of rolling stock, at the public transport premises. 49E Directions powers as to operation and movement of rolling stock and vehicles (1) If the Chief Investigator enters public transport premises, rolling stock or a bus under section 49B, the Chief Investigator may give a direction to any person at the premises or on the rolling stock or bus that relates to the stopping or movement of— (a) any road vehicle at the premises; or (b) the rolling stock or bus. (2) A person must not refuse or fail to comply with a direction under subsection (1) unless the person has a reasonable excuse. Penalty: 60 penalty units. 49F Directions powers in relation to vessels (1) If the Chief Investigator enters marine premises or boards, or proposes to board, a vessel under section 49B, the Chief Investigator may direct the master of a vessel or the person operating a vessel to do anything necessary to enable the effective and safe detention of the vessel. (2) The Chief Investigator, for the purpose of carrying out an investigation into a public transport safety matter or a marine safety matter, may direct the master of the vessel, or person operating the vessel, to— (a) stop the vessel; or (b) manoeuvre the vessel in a specified manner or to a specified place; or (c) secure the vessel in a specified manner; or (d) produce, for inspection, equipment specified in the direction. (3) A person must not refuse or fail to comply with a direction under subsection (1) or (2) unless the person has a reasonable excuse. Penalty: 60 penalty units. 49G Detention of vessels for 48 hours If the Chief Investigator boards a vessel under section 49B, the Chief Investigator may detain the vessel for so long as is necessary (but no longer than 48 hours) for the purposes of exercising a power under section 49D. 49H Magistrates' Court may extend period of detention of vessel (1) The Chief Investigator may apply to the Magistrates' Court for an extension of the period a vessel has been detained under section 49G. (2) An application must be made within the maximum 48 hour detention period permitted under section 49G or within a period extended by the Court under this section. (3) The Magistrates' Court may order such an extension if satisfied that the continued detention of a vessel is necessary— (a) for the purposes of an investigation into a marine safety matter; or (b) because the vessel is, or is likely to be, required for the purposes of an investigation into a marine safety matter. (4) The Court may adjourn an application to enable notice of the application to be given to any person. 49I Persons assisting the Chief Investigator (1) A person (the assistant), including an interpreter, may accompany the Chief Investigator in entering public transport premises or marine premises or other place, or rolling stock or bus or boarding a vessel under this Part to assist the Chief Investigator if the Chief Investigator considers the assistance necessary. (2) The assistant— (a) may do such things at the premises or place or on the rolling stock, bus or vessel and in such manner as the Chief Investigator reasonably requires to assist the Chief Investigator in the exercise of the Chief Investigator's powers under this Part; but (b) must not do anything that the Chief Investigator does not have power to do, except as permitted under a search warrant. (3) Anything done lawfully by the assistant is taken for all purposes to have been done by the Chief Investigator. 49J Use of electronic equipment (1) Without limiting section 49D, if— (a) a thing found at searchable premises or on a searchable rolling stock, bus or vessel is, or includes, a disk, tape or other device for the storage, receipt or transmission of information; and (b) the equipment at searchable premises or on a searchable rolling stock, bus or vessel, may be used with the disk, tape or other device— the Chief Investigator, or a person assisting the Chief Investigator, may operate the equipment to access the information. (2) If the Chief Investigator, or a person assisting the Chief Investigator, finds that a disk, tape, or other device for the storage, receipt or transmission of information at searchable premises or on a searchable rolling stock, bus or vessel contains information the Chief Investigator believes on reasonable grounds is relevant to an investigation into a public transport safety matter or marine safety matter, the Chief Investigator or person assisting the Chief Investigator may— (a) put the information in documentary form and seize the documents so produced; or (b) copy the information to another disk, tape or other storage device and remove that storage device from the searchable premises or searchable rolling stock, bus or vessel; or (c) if it is not practicable to put the information in documentary form nor to copy the information, seize the disk, tape or other storage device and the equipment that enables the information to be accessed. (3) The Chief Investigator, or a person assisting the Chief Investigator, must not operate or seize equipment for the purpose mentioned in this section unless the Chief Investigator or person assisting believes on reasonable grounds that the operation or seizure of the equipment can be carried out without damage to the equipment. (4) In this section— information has the same meaning as in the Electronic Transactions (Victoria) Act 2000. 49K Use of equipment to examine or process things (1) Without limiting section 49D, the Chief Investigator, in exercising a power under this Part, may bring to, onto, or into searchable premises or a searchable rolling stock, bus or vessel any equipment reasonably necessary for the examination or processing of things found at the premises or on or in the rolling stock, bus or vessel in order to determine whether they are things that may be seized. (2) The Chief Investigator, or a person assisting the Chief Investigator, may operate equipment already at searchable premises or on a searchable rolling stock, bus or vessel to carry out the examination or processing of a thing found in or at the premises or on or in the rolling stock, bus or vessel in order to determine whether it is a thing that may be seized, if the Chief Investigator or person assisting believes on reasonable grounds that— (a) the equipment is suitable for the examination or the processing; and (b) the examination or processing can be carried out without damage to the equipment. 49L Securing a site or restricting access to rolling stock, bus or vessel (1) For the purpose of protecting evidence that might be relevant for the purpose of carrying out an investigation into a public transport safety matter or a marine safety matter, the Chief Investigator or a police officer may— (a) secure the perimeter of any site at any place; or (b) restrict access to rolling stock, a bus or vessel. (2) The Chief Investigator or a police officer may secure the perimeter of a site or restrict access to rolling stock, a bus or vessel under subsection (1) by whatever means the Chief Investigator or the police officer considers appropriate. (3) A person must not, without the permission of the Chief Investigator or a police officer— (a) enter or remain at a site the perimeter of which is secured under this section; or (b) enter or board or remain on rolling stock, a bus or vessel access to which has been restricted under this section. Penalty: 60 penalty units. (4) Subsection (3) does not apply if the person— (a) enters or remains at the site or enters or boards or remains on the rolling stock, bus or vessel to ensure the safety of persons; or (b) enters or remains at the site or enters or boards or remains on the rolling stock, bus or vessel to remove deceased persons or animals from the site or bus or vessel; or (c) enters or remains at the site to move a road vehicle, or the wreckage of a road vehicle, to a safe place; or (d) enters or remains at the site or enters or boards or remains on the rolling stock, bus or vessel to protect the environment from significant damage or pollution. (5) The Chief Investigator or a police officer must not unreasonably withhold a permission referred to in subsection (3). 49M Directions for the protection of evidence (1) For the purpose of protecting evidence that might be relevant for the purpose of carrying out an investigation into a public transport safety matter or a marine safety matter, the Chief Investigator may direct the person in control of a specified thing or class of specified things that the specified thing, or class of specified things, must not be removed or interfered with except with the permission of the Chief Investigator. (2) A person must not fail or refuse to comply with a direction under subsection (1). Penalty: 60 penalty units. (3) Subsection (2) does not apply if the conduct concerned was necessary— (a) to ensure the safety of persons, animals or property; or (b) for the movement of deceased persons or animals; or (c) to move rolling stock or a bus, or the wreckage of rolling stock or a bus, to a safe place; or (d) to protect the environment from significant damage or pollution. (4) The Chief Investigator must not unreasonably withhold the Chief Investigator's permission under subsection (1). (5) In this section— in control, in relation to a thing or a specified class of things, means having, or reasonably appearing to the Chief Investigator as having, authority to exercise control over the thing or specified class of things. Division 4—Search warrants 49N Search warrants (1) The Chief Investigator may apply to a magistrate for a search warrant for a place, rolling stock, a bus or vessel. (2) The magistrate may refuse to consider the application until the Chief Investigator gives the magistrate all the information the magistrate requires about the application in the way the magistrate requires. (3) The magistrate may issue a search warrant only if the magistrate is satisfied there are reasonable grounds for suspecting— (a) there is a particular thing or activity (the evidence) that may be significant to an investigation into a public transport safety matter or a marine safety matter; and (b) the evidence is, or may be within the next 72 hours, at the place or on the rolling stock or on the bus or vessel. (4) The search warrant must state— (a) that the Chief Investigator may, with necessary and reasonable help and force, enter the place, rolling stock or bus, or board the vessel, and exercise the powers of the Chief Investigator; and (b) a brief description of the investigation in respect of which the warrant is sought; and (c) the evidence that may be seized under the search warrant; and (d) the hours of the day or night when the place, rolling stock or bus may be entered or vessel may be boarded; and (e) the date, within 7 days after the search warrant's issue, the search warrant ends. (5) A search warrant must be issued in accordance with the Magistrates' Court Act 1989 and in the form set out in the rules of court under that Act. (6) Despite section 78 of the Magistrates' Court Act 1989, a search warrant must not authorise the Chief Investigator to arrest a person. (7) Subject to any provision to the contrary in this Division, the rules to be observed with respect to search warrants mentioned in the Magistrates' Court Act 1989 extend and apply to warrants under this section. 49O Seizure of things not mentioned in the warrant A search warrant authorises the Chief Investigator, in addition to the seizure of any thing of the kind described in the warrant, to seize any thing which is not of the kind described in the warrant if— (a) the Chief Investigator believes, on reasonable grounds, that the thing— (i) is of a kind which could have been included in a warrant issued under this Part; or (ii) is of significance to an investigation into a public transport safety matter or a marine safety matter; and (b) the Chief Investigator believes, on reasonable grounds, that it is necessary to seize that thing in order to prevent its concealment, loss or destruction. 49P Announcement before entry or boarding on warrant (1) Before executing a search warrant, the Chief Investigator or an assistant to the Chief Investigator must— (a) announce that the Chief Investigator is authorised by the warrant to enter the place, rolling stock or bus or board the vessel; and (b) give any person at the place or on the rolling stock, bus or vessel an opportunity to allow that entry or boarding. (2) However, the Chief Investigator or an assistant to the Chief Investigator need not comply with subsection (1) if they believe on reasonable grounds that immediate entry to the place, or into the rolling stock or bus, or boarding of the vessel is needed to ensure— (a) the safety of any person; or (b) that the effective execution of the warrant is not frustrated. 49Q Copy of warrant to be given to person with control or management of place, rolling stock, bus or vessel If the person who has, or appears to have, control or management of a place, rolling stock, a bus or vessel is present at the place or on the rolling stock, bus or vessel when a search warrant is being executed, the Chief Investigator must— (a) produce the Chief Investigator's photo identification to that person for inspection; and (b) give that person a copy of the warrant. Division 5—Other related investigatory powers 49R Power to require production of documents and related items (1) The Chief Investigator may, for the purposes of an investigation into a public transport safety matter or a marine safety matter, direct a specified person to provide to the Chief Investigator— (a) any document required to be kept under a relevant transport safety or infrastructure law; and (b) any documents, devices or other things in the specified person's possession or control relating to— (i) the provision of bus services; or (ii) railway operations; or (iii) marine operations; and (c) any document that the Chief Investigator believes on reasonable grounds may contain information that is relevant for the purposes of the investigation into the transport safety matter or marine safety matter. (2) The direction must state where and to whom the documents, devices or other things are to be produced. (3) In giving a direction, the Chief Investigator may specify particular documents, devices or other things, or particular classes of documents, devices or other things. (4) The Chief Investigator may do any or all of the following— (a) inspect any documents, devices or other things that are produced; (b) copy any documents, devices or other things that are produced; (c) seize and remove any documents, devices or other things that are produced that the Chief Investigator believes on reasonable grounds are significant for the purposes of the investigation into the public transport safety matter or marine safety matter. (5) A person must not, without reasonable excuse, fail to comply with a requirement under this section. Penalty: In the case of a natural person, 20 penalty units; In the case of a body corporate, 100 penalty units. 49S Power to require persons to attend and answer questions (1) If the Chief Investigator considers it necessary for the purposes of an investigation into a public transport safety matter or a marine safety matter, the Chief Investigator may require a person to attend before the Chief Investigator and answer questions asked by the Chief Investigator relating to matters relevant to the investigation. (2) The requirement under subsection (1) must be by notice in writing. (3) The notice must— (a) be signed by the Chief Investigator; and (b) specify the time and place at which the person is required to attend before the Chief Investigator. (4) The time specified in the notice must be reasonable having regard to the circumstances. (5) When a person attends before the Chief Investigator under this section, the Chief Investigator may require the questions to be answered on oath or affirmation. (6) For the purposes of subsection (5), the Chief Investigator may administer an oath or affirmation. (7) A person of whom a requirement is made under this section must not— (a) fail to attend before the Chief Investigator in accordance with the requirement; or (b) refuse to take an oath or make an affirmation when required by the Chief Investigator to do so; or (c) refuse or fail to answer a question lawfully asked of the person by the Chief Investigator. Penalty: 30 penalty units. (8) A person who attends before the Chief Investigator in accordance with a requirement under this section is entitled to be paid, in relation to that attendance, fees or allowances fixed by or calculated in accordance with an Order made by the Governor in Council for the purposes of this section. 49T Abrogation of privilege against self‑incrimination (1) A person is not excused from answering a question or providing information or a document under this Part on the ground that the answer to the question, or the information or document, may tend to incriminate the person or expose the person to a penalty. (2) However— (a) any answer to a question or information or a document provided by a person under this Part is not admissible as evidence against that person in a criminal proceeding or a proceeding for the imposition of a civil penalty other than— (i) a proceeding arising out of the false or misleading nature of the answer, information or document; or (ii) a proceeding in respect of an offence against section 49S; and (b) any information provided or document obtained as a direct result or indirect consequence of the answer, information or document being provided by a natural person under a requirement or direction under this Part is not admissible as evidence against that person in a criminal proceeding or a proceeding for the imposition of a civil penalty other than a proceeding arising out of the false and misleading nature of the answer, information or document. 49U Warning to be given Before requiring a person to answer a question or provide information or a document under this Part, the Chief Investigator must— (a) warn the person that failure to comply with the requirement or to answer the question may constitute an offence; and (b) warn the person about the effect of section 49T; and (c) advise the person about the effect of section 127. 49V Refusal on self-incrimination grounds not offence if warning not given It is not an offence for a natural person to refuse to answer a question put by the Chief Investigator or provide information or a document to the Chief Investigator under this Part on the ground that the question, information or document might tend to incriminate the person, unless the person was first given the warning under section 49U(a). 49W Power to copy and retain documents The Chief Investigator may— (a) make copies of, or take extracts from, a document given to the Chief Investigator in accordance with a requirement under a transport safety or infrastructure law or seized under this Part; and (b) keep that document for the period that the Chief Investigator considers necessary. 49X Inspecting and copying documents in custody of the Chief Investigator under this Part While the Chief Investigator retains custody of a document, the Chief Investigator must permit the following persons to inspect or make copies of the document at all reasonable times— (a) the person who produced the document; (b) the owner of the document; (c) a person authorised by a person referred to in paragraph (a) or (b). 49Y Securing seized things On seizing a thing under this Part, the Chief Investigator may— (a) move the thing from the public transport premises, marine premises, place, rolling stock, bus or vessel where it was seized (the place of seizure); or (b) leave the thing at the place of seizure but take steps to restrict access to it; or (c) in relation to equipment that is seized, make the equipment inoperable. 49Z Offence to tamper with seized thing (1) If the Chief Investigator restricts access to a seized thing, a person must not tamper, or attempt to tamper, with the thing, or something restricting access to the thing, without the Chief Investigator's permission. Penalty: 60 penalty units. (2) If the Chief Investigator makes seized equipment inoperable, a person must not tamper, or attempt to tamper, with the equipment, without the Chief Investigator's permission. Penalty: 60 penalty units. 49ZA Directions relating to seizure (1) To enable a thing to be seized under this Part, the Chief Investigator may direct the person in control of it— (a) to take it to a specified place within a specified time; and (b) if necessary, to remain in control of it at the specified place for a period specified in the direction. (2) A direction under subsection (1)— (a) must be given by signed written notice given to the person; or (b) if for any reason it is not practicable to give signed written notice to the person—may be given orally and confirmed by signed written notice given to the person as soon as is practicable. (3) A further direction may be made under this section about the thing if it is necessary and reasonable to make the further direction. (4) A person given a direction under subsection (1) or (3) must comply with that direction unless the person has a reasonable excuse. Penalty: 20 penalty units. (5) Without limiting what may otherwise be a reasonable excuse under subsection (4), it is a reasonable excuse for a person in control of a thing not to comply with a direction under subsection (1) or (3) if, in all the circumstances, the direction was unreasonable. (6) The cost of complying with a direction under subsection (1) or (3) must be borne by the person. (7) In this section— in control, in relation to a thing, means having, or reasonably appearing to the Chief Investigator as having, authority to exercise control over the thing. 49ZB Chief Investigator may direct a thing's return (1) If the Chief Investigator has directed a person to take a thing to a specified place within a specified time under section 49ZA(1), the Chief Investigator may direct the person to return the thing to the place from which it was taken. (2) A person given a direction under subsection (1) must comply with that direction unless the person has a reasonable excuse. Penalty: 20 penalty units. (3) Without limiting what may otherwise be a reasonable excuse under subsection (2), it is a reasonable excuse for a person not to comply with a direction under subsection (1) if, in all the circumstances, the direction was unreasonable. (4) The cost of complying with a direction under subsection (1) must be borne by the person. 49ZC Receipt for seized things (1) After the Chief Investigator seizes a thing under this Part, the Chief Investigator must give a receipt for it to the person from whom the thing was seized or the owner of the thing. (2) However, if for any reason it is not practicable to comply with subsection (1), the Chief Investigator must leave the receipt in a conspicuous position and in a reasonably secure way— (a) at the place of seizure; or (b) if the thing was seized from rolling stock, a bus or vessel, on the rolling stock, bus or vessel. (3) The receipt must describe generally the thing seized and its condition. (4) This section does not apply if it would be impracticable or unreasonable to expect the Chief Investigator to account for the thing, given its condition, nature and value. 49ZD Copies of certain seized things to be given (1) If, under this Part, the Chief Investigator seizes— (a) a document; or (b) a thing that can be readily copied; or (c) a storage device containing information that can be readily copied— the Chief Investigator must give a copy of the thing or information to the owner or custodian of the document, thing or device as soon as practicable after the seizure. (2) Subsection (1) does not apply— (a) to any document, thing or device moved under section 49Y(a) or 49ZA; or (b) if the Chief Investigator is unable to discover the identity of the owner or custodian of any document, thing or device seized. 49ZE Forfeiture of seized things (1) A thing seized under this Part is forfeited to the State if the Chief Investigator— (a) cannot find the person entitled to the thing after making reasonable inquiries; or (b) cannot return it to the person entitled to it, after making reasonable efforts; or (c) reasonably believes it is necessary to forfeit the thing for the purpose of carrying out an investigation into a public transport safety matter or a marine safety matter. (2) Subsection (1)(a) does not require the Chief Investigator to make inquiries if it would be unreasonable to make inquiries to find the person entitled to the thing. (3) Subsection (1)(b) does not require the Chief Investigator to make efforts if it would be unreasonable to make efforts to return the thing to the person entitled to it. (4) If the Chief Investigator decides to forfeit the thing under subsection (1)(c), the Chief Investigator must tell the person entitled to the thing of the decision by written notice. (5) Subsection (4) does not apply if— (a) the Chief Investigator cannot find the person entitled to the thing after making reasonable inquiries; or (b) it is impracticable or would be unreasonable to give the notice. (6) The notice must state— (a) the reasons for the decision; and (b) information about the right of review under Part 5. (7) In deciding whether and, if so, what inquiries and efforts are reasonable or whether it would be unreasonable to give notice about a thing, regard must be had to the thing's nature, condition and value. (8) Any costs reasonably incurred by the Chief Investigator in storing or disposing of a thing forfeited under subsection (1)(c) may be recovered in a court of competent jurisdiction as a debt due to the Chief Investigator from the person entitled. (9) In this section— person entitled to a thing means the person from whom it was seized unless that person is not entitled to possess it in which case it means the owner of the thing. 49ZF Return of seized things (1) If a seized thing has not been forfeited under this Part, the person entitled to the thing may apply to the Chief Investigator for the return of the thing after the end of 6 months after it was seized. (2) The Chief Investigator must return the thing to the applicant under subsection (1) unless the Chief Investigator has reasonable grounds to retain the thing. (3) For the purposes of subsection (2), a reasonable ground to retain the thing is for the purpose of carrying out an investigation into a public transport safety matter or a marine safety matter. (4) The Chief Investigator may impose any conditions on the return of the thing under this section that the Chief Investigator considers appropriate to eliminate or minimise any risk to safety related to the thing. (5) In this section— person entitled to a thing means the person entitled to possess the thing or the owner of the thing. 49ZG Access to seized thing (1) Until a thing seized under this Part is forfeited or returned under this Part, the Chief Investigator must allow its owner to inspect it and, if it is a document, to copy it. (2) Subsection (1) does not apply if it is impracticable or it would be unreasonable to allow the inspection or copying. Division 6—Damage and compensation 49ZH Damage etc to be minimised In the exercise, or purported exercise, of a power under this Part, the Chief Investigator must take all reasonable steps to ensure that the Chief Investigator, and any assistant to the Chief Investigator, cause as little inconvenience, detriment and damage as is practicable. 49ZI Chief Investigator to give notice of damage (1) This section applies if the Chief Investigator or an assistant to the Chief Investigator damages a thing when exercising or purporting to exercise a power under this Part. (2) The Chief Investigator must, as soon as practicable, give written notice of the damage to the person whom the Chief Investigator believes on reasonable grounds is the person in control of the thing. (3) If the Chief Investigator believes the damage was caused by a latent defect in the thing or circumstances beyond the Chief Investigator's or assistant's control, the Chief Investigator may state it in the notice. (4) If, for any reason, it is impracticable to comply with subsection (2), the Chief Investigator must leave the notice in a conspicuous position and in a reasonably secure way where the damage happened. (5) This section does not apply to damage the Chief Investigator reasonably believes is trivial. 49ZJ Compensation (1) A person may claim compensation from the Chief Investigator if the person incurs damage because of the exercise or purported exercise of a power under this Part. (2) In determining the amount of compensation payable in relation to any damage caused to electronic equipment, regard is to be had to whether the occupier of the public transport premises or marine premises and the employees and agents of the occupier, if they were available at the time, had provided any warning or guidance as to the operation of the equipment that was appropriate in the circumstances. 49ZK Limits on compensation The Chief Investigator is not liable to pay compensation to a person for any damage caused during any inspection or search conducted under this Part, or under a search warrant executed in accordance with this Part, if the damage caused was no more than was reasonably necessary in inspecting, or searching for, the thing. 49ZL Compensation may be claimed as part of a court proceeding (1) Compensation may be claimed and ordered in a proceeding commenced in a court of competent jurisdiction. (2) The court may order compensation to be paid only if it is satisfied it is just to make the order in the circumstances of the particular case. (3) The regulations may prescribe matters that may, or must, be taken into account by the court when considering whether it is just to make the order. Division 7—Directions powers 49ZM Chief Investigator may require name and address (1) The Chief Investigator may require a person to provide the person's name and residential address if the Chief Investigator believes, on reasonable grounds, that the person is a specified person. (2) When asking a person to provide the person's name and residential address, the Chief Investigator must— (a) tell the person the reason for the requirement to provide the person's name and residential address; and (b) warn the person that it is an offence to fail to state that name and residential address, unless the person has a reasonable excuse. (3) If the Chief Investigator reasonably believes that the name or residential address is false, the Chief Investigator may require the person to give evidence of its correctness. (4) A person must not, without reasonable excuse, fail to comply with a requirement under subsection (1) or (3). Penalty: 20 penalty units. 49ZN Direction to provide certain information (1) The Chief Investigator may direct, for the purpose of carrying out an investigation into a public transport safety matter or a marine safety matter— (a) a rail operator or a rail safety worker who is associated with particular rolling stock— (i) to state the name, home address and business address of any other person who is associated with the rolling stock; and (ii) to give any information that is within the power of the person to give that may lead to the identification of the owner or operator of the rolling stock on any occasion; or (b) a provider of a bus service or a bus safety worker who is associated with a particular bus— (i) to state the name, home address and business address of any other person who is associated with the bus; and (ii) to give any information that is within the power of the person to give that may lead to the identification of the owner or operator of the bus on any occasion; or (c) a person whom the Chief Investigator believes has information concerning the identity or location of the owner or master of a vessel to provide all the information the person has regarding the identity and location of the owner and master of the vessel. (2) A person must not refuse or fail to comply with a direction under subsection (1). Penalty: 20 penalty units. (3) It is not an offence for a person to fail to comply with subsection (2) if the Chief Investigator did not inform the person, at the time the direction was made, that it is an offence to fail to comply with the direction. (4) In this section— associated with means the owner or operator of, or in charge or apparently in charge of. 49ZO Manner in which the Chief Investigator may give directions under this Part (1) The Chief Investigator may give a direction under this Part orally or in writing. (2) If giving a direction orally, the Chief Investigator must— (a) state whether it is to be complied with immediately or within a specified period; and (b) warn the person to whom the direction is given that it is an offence under this Act to fail to comply with a direction. (3) If giving a direction in writing, the Chief Investigator must ensure that the direction— (a) states the period within which it is to be complied with; and (b) states that it is an offence under this Act to fail to comply with a direction. (4) A written direction may be given to, or sent by post to, the person to whom it is directed. 49ZP Directions may be given under more than one provision (1) The Chief Investigator may, on the same occasion, give directions under one or more provisions of this Part. (2) Without limiting subsection (1), the Chief Investigator, in the course of exercising powers under a provision of this Part, may do either or both of the following— (a) give further directions under the provision; (b) give further directions under one or more other provisions of this Part. Division 8—Other investigatory matters 49ZQ Chief Investigator to carry photo identification The Chief Investigator must carry photo identification when exercising a power under this Part. 49ZR Production of photo identification (1) The Chief Investigator must produce the Chief Investigator's photo identification for inspection— (a) before exercising a power under this Part; or (b) if asked to do so by any person at any time during the exercise of a power under this Part. (2) However, the Chief Investigator need not produce the Chief Investigator's photo identification when asked to do so if— (a) the Chief Investigator reasonably believes that the production of the Chief Investigator's photo identification would— (i) affect the safety or welfare of any person; or (ii) frustrate the effective exercise of a power under this Part; or (b) the request to produce the Chief Investigator's photo identification is made by a person to whom the Chief Investigator has already produced that identification on the same day. (3) Any action taken or thing done by the Chief Investigator under this Part is not invalidated if the Chief Investigator fails to produce the Chief Investigator's photo identification. 49ZS Identity cards (1) If the Chief Investigator delegates any power conferred on the Chief Investigator by this Part to another person, the Chief Investigator must give the person an identity card that contains a photograph of the person and that identifies the person by name as a person authorised to exercise the power by the Chief Investigator. (2) If a person to whom an identity card has been issued under subsection (1) ceases to be authorised to exercise any power referred to in the identity card, the person must return the identity card to the Chief Investigator as soon as is practicable after that cessation. Penalty: 1 penalty unit. 49ZT Residential premises Despite anything else in this Part, the powers of the Chief Investigator under this Part in relation to entering a place, rolling stock or bus or boarding a vessel are not exercisable in respect of any part of the place, rolling stock, bus or vessel that are residential premises except— (a) with the consent of— (i) the person with control or management of the residential premises; or (ii) a person at the premises; or (iii) a resident of the premises; or (b) under the authority conferred by a search warrant; or (c) for the sole purpose of gaining access to suspected public transport premises, but only— (i) if the Chief Investigator reasonably believes that no reasonable alternative access is available; and (ii) at a reasonable time, having regard to the times at which the Chief Investigator believes rail safety work or bus safety work is being carried out at the premises to which access is sought. 49ZU Use of force A power conferred under this Part to enter a place, rolling stock or bus or board a vessel, or to do anything in or on that place or on that rolling stock, bus or vessel, may not be exercised unless the Chief Investigator or a person assisting the Chief Investigator, uses no more force than is reasonably necessary to effect the entry or boarding or to do the thing for which the entry or boarding is effected. 49ZV Power to use force against persons to be exercised only by police officers A provision in this Part that authorises a person to use reasonable force does not authorise a person who is not a police officer to use force against another person. 49ZW Manner in which Chief Investigator must exercise powers In exercising powers under this Part, the Chief Investigator must— (a) cause as little inconvenience as possible; and (b) not remain at any place or on any rolling stock, bus or vessel any longer than is reasonably necessary. 49ZX Information given voluntarily Nothing in this Part prevents the Chief Investigator from obtaining and using evidence given to the Chief Investigator voluntarily by any person. Division 9—Reports and miscellaneous matters 49ZY Reports to be given promptly to the Minister The Chief Investigator must, as soon as is practicable after completing an investigation into a public transport safety matter or marine safety matter, give the Minister a report of the investigation. 49ZZ Consultation before report finalised Before giving a report to the Minister under section 49ZY, the Chief Investigator must consult with— (a) Safe Transport Victoria; and (b) the Secretary; and (c) the Head, Transport for Victoria; and (d) any person or body who has assisted the Chief Investigator with the investigation; and (e) any person or body to whom the report may be relevant. 49ZZA Publication of investigation-related materials (1) The Chief Investigator may publish, by electronic or other means, investigation‑related materials if the Chief Investigator considers that the publication of the materials is necessary or desirable for the purposes of transport safety. (2) Published investigation-related materials may only include information that is, or that contains, personal information in the circumstances allowed by the regulations. (3) In this section, investigation-related materials means— (a) a report given to the Minister under section 49ZY; or (b) a summary of a report given to the Minister under section 49ZY; or (c) safety advisory statements; or (d) safety recommendations; or (e) any other document relating to an investigation into a public transport safety matter or marine safety matter. 49ZZB Limitations on disclosure etc of information obtained under this Part (1) A person must not disclose any information obtained while carrying out a function under this Part, or obtained under section 49ZZE. Penalty: 60 penalty units. (2) However, the person may disclose such information if— (a) the disclosure is made in the performance of a duty under, or in connection with, this Part; or (b) the person has the consent of the person who originally supplied the information; or (c) subject to subsection (3), the disclosure is made in legal proceedings at the direction of a court; or (d) the information is in the public domain at the time it is disclosed. (3) A court may only direct a person to disclose the information if— (a) the disclosure is required for the purposes of a criminal proceeding for an offence against this Act; or (b) the disclosure is to be made in civil proceedings and the following 2 conditions are met— (i) the Chief Investigator has issued a certificate in relation to the information stating that the disclosure of the information is not likely to interfere with any investigation; and (ii) the court is satisfied that any adverse domestic and international impact that the disclosure of the information might have on any current or future investigations is outweighed by the public interest in the administration of justice. (4) In directing a person to disclose information, the court may also direct that the information, or any information obtained from the information, must not— (a) be published, or be communicated to any person; or (b) be published, or be communicated, except in a manner, and to a person, specified by the court. (5) Any information disclosed by a person in contravention of this section is not admissible in any civil or criminal proceeding (other than a proceeding against the person under this section). (6) Subsection (2) is not intended to interfere with any rights another person may have with regard to the disclosure of the information. (7) A reference in this section to a court is to be read as including a reference to a tribunal and to a person exercising judicial authority. 49ZZC Release of information in the interests of transport safety (1) The Chief Investigator may disclose information acquired by the Chief Investigator in carrying out the Chief Investigator's functions under this or any other Act to any person if the Chief Investigator considers that the disclosure is necessary or desirable for the purposes of transport safety. (2) However, the Chief Investigator may only disclose information that is, or that contains, personal information in the circumstances allowed by the regulations. 49ZZD Reports not admissible in evidence (1) A report of an investigation into a public transport safety matter or marine safety matter under this Part is not admissible in evidence in any civil or criminal proceeding. (2) Subsection (1) does not apply— (a) to the admissibility of a final report in evidence in a coronial inquiry; or (b) if the court considers that a failure to admit a report into evidence in a criminal proceeding could prejudice the fair trial of the accused. (3) This section applies despite anything to the contrary in sections 49ZZB and 49ZZC. (4) In this section report means— (a) final report; or (b) draft report; or (c) any document that is incidental to a final report or draft report. 49ZZE Chief Investigator may authorise non-staff members to have access to information The Chief Investigator may authorise a person who is not a member of the Chief Investigator's staff to have access to information acquired by the Chief Investigator in carrying out the Chief Investigator's functions under this or any other Act if the Chief Investigator considers that it is necessary or desirable to do so. 49ZZF Confidential reporting of safety information by transport workers (1) The Chief Investigator may establish a system for the voluntary reporting by transport workers of public transport safety matters and marine safety matters. (2) The Chief Investigator must not disclose to any other person, or to any court, tribunal or person acting judicially, any information that may identify a transport worker who provides information under the voluntary reporting system unless— (a) the worker consents to the disclosure; or (b) the Chief Investigator or the court, tribunal or person is of the opinion that it is necessary in the public interest that the information be disclosed. (3) In this section a transport worker is a person who, as an employee, as a contractor or as a volunteer— (a) carries out work for— (i) a person who operates a commercial bus service (within the meaning of section 3(1) of the Bus Safety Act 2009); or (ii) a person who manages any rail infrastructure or who provides, or operates, any rolling stock; or (iii) a person who undertakes rail safety work; or (b) is involved with the operation of vessels. 49ZZG Chief Investigator may ask Commonwealth agency to investigate accident or incident The Chief Investigator may ask the Australian Transport Safety Bureau established under section 12 of the Transport Safety Investigation Act 2003 of the Commonwealth to investigate any accident or incident that has occurred in Victoria that is a public transport safety matter or a marine safety matter.".
